title: Remote Patient Monitoring: Scaling Proactive Care in Rural Vermont
summary: This analysis evaluates the Vermont RPM Grant Program's role in shifting healthcare from reactive, high-cost episodes to proactive, home-based monitoring. It explores the technical integration of real-time physiological data to improve chronic disease management and institutional efficiency.

children.text: The Shift Toward Proactive Care Infrastructure

The RPM Grant Program is designed to equip provider organizations—specifically home health agencies, primary care practices, and community paramedicine units—with the hardware and software necessary to monitor patients outside of clinical settings. By collecting real-time physiological data, clinicians can intervene earlier, preventing the deterioration of chronic conditions that typically lead to expensive emergency department visits.

children.text: Success in these programs relies on the transition toward digital health infrastructure that supports data liquidity and interoperability. By providing capital grants for rural organizations, the program addresses the economic barriers to adopting technology that serves as a critical safety net for high-risk populations.
